newsitem.title: AFGHANISTAN: Taleban, opposition trade claims on fighting.
newsitem.headline: Taleban, opposition trade claims on fighting.

text.p: The Islamic Taleban movement said on Monday it had defeated its foes in eastern provinces of Afghanistan and did not see them as any threat to its rule.

"The revolts of the opponents of the Islamic State (of Afghanistan) have been all defeated and there is no longer any possible danger," Amir Khan Mutaqi, the Taleban information and culture minister, told reporters.
He was responding to an opposition report on Saturday, which said opposition forces had killed nine Taleban fighters while repelling an attack in Kunar province, northeast of Kabul.

But Afghan sources quoted by the Pakistan-based Afghan Islamic Press (AIP) said forces led by Abdullah Jan, former governor of Laghman province, were holding the town of Tarang, nine km (six miles) from the provincial capital of Mehtar Lam.
The sources said Taleban artillery had been in action for the past two days as part of efforts to recapture Tarang. They said fighting was continuing in Kunar, but had no details.

Factions loyal to former president Burhanuddin Rabbani have recently launched attacks on the Taleban in eastern provinces captured by the purist Islamic militia last year, but Mutaqi said the opposition was much weaker than it claimed.

"Their threats are completely over in Nangarhar and the situation is calm in Laghman. There is no danger in Kunar either, but occasionally the hideouts of the enemy are firing shells from the mountains," he said.
"They are no longer able to launch any offensive and they make false news to boost the morale of their fighters."
Mutaqi said the Taleban had taken about 300 opposition prisoners in Nangarhar and Laghman provinces recently, including the son of former Nangarhar governor Haji Qadir.

AIP quoted Taleban sources as saying that information provided by Haji Qadir's son, Mohammad Zahir, had enabled the Taleban to seize large amounts of weapons and ammunition in the Surkh Rud area, 10 km (six miles) west of Jalalabad, on Friday.
